# NeuroBrix CLI reference

<!-- Generated by tools/cli_reference.py from the `neurobrix` argument parser. Do not edit by hand: regenerate with `PYTHONPATH=src python tools/cli_reference.py`. -->

Every command, flag, default and help text below is read from the command-line parser itself. How the commands are used, family by family, is in [CLI usage](../cli_usage.md); serving, chat and the HTTP API in [Serving and chat](../serving.md).

A default of `—` means the value comes from elsewhere: the model's container, its family's defaults, the hardware profile, or the command's own behaviour described in the flag's text.

## Commands

| command | description |
|---|---|
| [`run`](#run) | Run inference using NBX Engine |
| [`info`](#info) | Display system information |
| [`inspect`](#inspect) | Inspect a .nbx file or an installed model |
| [`import`](#import) | Download model from NeuroBrix registry |
| [`list`](#list) | List installed models |
| [`remove`](#remove) | Remove a model (cache, store, or both) |
| [`clean`](#clean) | Wipe all downloaded models (store and/or cache) |
| [`hub`](#hub) | Browse models on the NeuroBrix registry |
| [`serve`](#serve) | Start persistent model serving daemon |
| [`chat`](#chat) | Interactive chat with running daemon |
| [`stop`](#stop) | Stop the serving daemon and free VRAM |
| [`doctor`](#doctor) | Diagnose installation problems (PATH, PyTorch/CUDA, GPU visibility) |
| [`validate`](#validate) | Validate NBX file integrity |
| [`upscale`](#upscale) | Upscale an image using a super-resolution model |

Developer commands (`neurobrix --help -v`):

| command | description |
|---|---|
| [`calibrate`](#calibrate) | Measure the precision calibration record of a model (DtypeEngine fp32 islands) |
| [`autotune`](#autotune) | The certified autotune directory: certify a profile, check the directory, show the status |
| [`drift`](#drift) | Name the first op where the Triton engine drifts from the ATen oracle on one request |
| [`coverage`](#coverage) | Which installed containers actually reach a symbol |

## Global options

```
neurobrix [options] <command> ...
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--version` | — | show program's version number and exit |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | 0 | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

## run

Run inference using NBX Engine.

Run inference using Prism ExecutionPlan + NBX Engine. Family is read from manifest.

```
neurobrix run [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` `MODEL` | — | Model name (auto-detected from running daemon if omitted) |
| `--hardware` `HARDWARE` | — | Hardware profile ID (e.g., "v100-32g"). Auto-detected if omitted. |
| `--explain-plan` | off | Print the placement plan — the strategy, why it won and what it beat, every component with its device and memory — then exit without loading anything |
| `--json` | off | with --explain-plan: the plan as one JSON record on stdout |
| `--prompt` `PROMPT` | — | Text prompt for generation |
| `--audio` `AUDIO` | — | Input audio file path (for speech-to-text models) |
| `--steps` `STEPS` | — | Number of inference steps |
| `--cfg` `CFG` | — | Guidance scale |
| `--height` `HEIGHT` | — | Output height in pixels |
| `--width` `WIDTH` | — | Output width in pixels |
| `--output` `OUTPUT` | — | Output file path (default: output.png) |
| `--seed` `SEED` | — | Random seed for reproducibility |
| `--temperature` `TEMPERATURE` | — | Sampling temperature (0 = greedy) |
| `--repetition-penalty` `REPETITION_PENALTY` | — | Repetition penalty (1.0 = none, 1.1-1.5 recommended) |
| `--top-k` `TOP_K` | — | Keep only the k highest-probability tokens (0 = disabled) |
| `--top-p` `TOP_P` | — | Nucleus sampling: keep the smallest set of tokens whose probability sums to p (1.0 = disabled) |
| `--set` `KEY=VALUE` | — | Set arbitrary runtime variable (e.g., --set global.cfg=7.5) |
| `--compiled` | off | PyTorch fused graph + cuDNN/cuBLAS (CompiledSequence). Production PyTorch performance. Used when no execution flag is passed and PyTorch is installed (without it, --triton); this flag makes the choice explicit. |
| `--sequential` | off | PyTorch eager op-by-op (no fusion, ATen dispatcher). Useful for debugging individual ATen ops. Slower than --compiled. |
| `--triton` | off | Triton-pure compiled mode: every op runs on NeuroBrix's own Triton kernels, with no cuDNN or cuBLAS, through a preallocated memory arena and fused kernels (TritonSequence). Needs the triton package. |
| `--triton-sequential` | off | Triton-pure eager mode: Triton kernels op-by-op (no fusion, TritonSequentialDispatcher). Equivalent of --sequential but for the Triton backend. Useful for debugging individual Triton kernels. |
| `--certified-only` | off | Confirmation run: every autotuned kernel is served from the certified directory, or the run fails naming the missing key and its census row — never a runtime sweep, never the local replay cache (NBX_AUTOTUNE_CERTIFIED_ONLY=1). |
| `--max-tokens` `MAX_TOKENS` | — | Maximum number of tokens to generate (LLM only) |
| `--turns` `FILE` | — | A JSON list of user messages played as ONE chat session, turn after turn, through the session code the daemon runs: the KV cache is kept between turns and each turn prefills only its new tokens; each answer is printed (LLM only) |
| `--input-image` `INPUT_IMAGE` | — | Input image path (vlm, img2img, inpainting, upscaler, multimodal) |
| `--input-video` `INPUT_VIDEO` | — | Input video path for understanding (vlm/multimodal) |
| `--mask-image` `MASK_IMAGE` | — | Inpainting mask image path (image inpainting mode) |
| `--reference-image` `REFERENCE_IMAGE` | — | Style reference image (not wired in this version: refused by name) |
| `--reference-audio` `REFERENCE_AUDIO` | — | Voice to clone from a recording (not wired in this version: refused by name) |
| `--speaker` `SPEAKER` | — | Speaker preset id (tts) |
| `--video` `VIDEO` | — | Input video path (video v2v) |
| `--num-frames` `NUM_FRAMES` | — | Number of frames to generate (video) |
| `--fps` `FPS` | — | Output frame rate (video) |
| `--system` `SYSTEM` | — | System prompt for chat-style models (llm, vlm, audio_llm) |
| `--mode` `{auto,text,chat,image,audio,video,t2i,img2img,inpainting,t2v,i2v,v2v}` | — | Execution mode. Required for multimodal (text\|image). Auto-deduced for other families from inputs provided. |
| `--chat` | — | Force chat template formatting |
| `--no-chat` | off | Force raw text completion |
| `--profile-kernels` `JSON` | — | Time every GPU kernel of the request on its own (Metal) and print them ranked by GPU time (with JSON: the whole table written there); each kernel runs alone, so the table ranks kernels and is not the run's speed |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

## inspect

Inspect a .nbx file or an installed model.

Show contents and metadata of a .nbx container. Accepts either a path to a .nbx file or the name of an installed model.

```
neurobrix inspect [options] PATH_OR_MODEL
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH_OR_MODEL` | required | Path to a .nbx file, or an installed model name |
| `--topology` | off | Show topology details |
| `--weights` | off | Show weight statistics |
| `--json` | off | one JSON record on stdout, human lines on stderr (schema in neurobrix/cli/json_out.py) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

## import

Download model from NeuroBrix registry.

Download a .nbx model from neurobrix.org and extract to local cache

```
neurobrix import [options] model_ref
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `model_ref` | required | Model reference: org/name (e.g., TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0) |
| `--registry` `REGISTRY` | — | Registry URL (default: https://neurobrix.org) |
| `--force` | off | Re-download even if already cached |
| `--no-keep` | off | Delete .nbx from store after extraction (saves disk space) |
| `--container` `FILE.nbx` | — | Install from (or record the name of an entry installed from) a container this machine already holds, verified against the sha256 the hub serves; nothing is downloaded |
| `--accept-license` | off | Record acceptance of the model license non-interactively (for scripts/CI; equivalent: NBX_ACCEPT_LICENSE=1) |
| `--json` | off | One NDJSON event per phase on stdout (info, license, download with byte counts, downloaded, extracting, installed, done \| error); human lines on stderr |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

```text
Examples:
  neurobrix import TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0
  neurobrix import hexgrad/Kokoro-82M

Run `neurobrix hub` to list every model the registry serves.
```

## remove

Remove a model (cache, store, or both).

Remove a model from cache, store, or both.

```
neurobrix remove [options] model_name
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `model_name` | required | Model name to remove (e.g., Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_1600M_1024px_MultiLing_diffusers) |
| `--store` | off | Remove from store only (keep cache) |
| `--all` | off | Remove from both cache and store |
| `--json` | off | One JSON record of what was removed on stdout; human lines on stderr |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

```text
Examples:
  neurobrix remove Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_1600M_1024px_MultiLing_diffusers             # Cache only (default)
  neurobrix remove Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_1600M_1024px_MultiLing_diffusers --store     # Store only (.nbx archive)
  neurobrix remove Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_1600M_1024px_MultiLing_diffusers --all       # Both cache and store
```

## clean

Wipe all downloaded models (store and/or cache).

Completely remove all models from ~/.neurobrix/store/ and/or ~/.neurobrix/cache/

```
neurobrix clean [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--store` | off | Delete all .nbx files from store/ |
| `--cache` | off | Delete all extracted models from cache/ |
| `--all` | off | Delete both store and cache |
| `-y`, `--yes` | off | Skip confirmation prompt |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

## hub

Browse models on the NeuroBrix registry.

List all models available for download on neurobrix.org

```
neurobrix hub [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--category`, `-c` `CATEGORY` | — | Filter by category. Any category the registry serves is accepted; an invalid value prints the valid ones. |
| `--search`, `-s` `SEARCH` | — | Search models by name, tag, or description |
| `--registry` `REGISTRY` | — | Registry URL (default: https://neurobrix.org) |
| `--json` | off | one JSON record on stdout, human lines on stderr (schema in neurobrix/cli/json_out.py) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

```text
Examples:
  neurobrix hub                        # List all models
  neurobrix hub --category IMAGE       # Filter by category
  neurobrix hub --search sana          # Search by name/tag
  neurobrix hub --category LLM -s chat # LLM models matching "chat"
```

## serve

Start persistent model serving daemon.

Load model weights into VRAM and serve requests via Unix socket.

```
neurobrix serve [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` `MODEL` | required | Model name |
| `--hardware` `HARDWARE` | — | Hardware profile ID. Auto-detected if omitted. |
| `--timeout` `TIMEOUT` | `1800` | Idle timeout in seconds (default: 1800) |
| `--foreground` | off | Run in foreground (block terminal, for debugging) |
| `--ready-fd` `READY_FD` | — | POSIX: an inherited pipe fd; the ready record (one JSON line) is written there once the daemon accepts, then the fd is closed |
| `--http` | off | Also serve the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API (/v1/...) on this daemon (default address: serving.http_host:http_port in config/system.yml) |
| `--http-host` `HTTP_HOST` | — | Address of the HTTP API (with --http); a non-loopback one needs --api-key-file |
| `--http-port` `HTTP_PORT` | — | Port of the HTTP API (with --http) |
| `--api-key-file` `API_KEY_FILE` | — | A file holding the API key the HTTP API requires (Authorization: Bearer) |
| `--ready-file` `READY_FILE` | — | A file the ready record (one JSON line) is written to, whole, once the daemon accepts (the Windows launcher reads it there) |
| `--compiled` | off | PyTorch fused graph + cuDNN/cuBLAS (the default where PyTorch is installed) |
| `--sequential` | off | PyTorch eager op-by-op (no fusion, debug) |
| `--triton` | off | Triton-pure compiled mode (NeuroBrix Triton kernels) |
| `--triton-sequential` | off | Triton-pure eager op-by-op (debug Triton) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

```text
Examples:
  neurobrix serve --model TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 --hardware v100-32g
  neurobrix serve --model TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 --hardware v100-32g --timeout 3600
```

## chat

Interactive chat with running daemon.

Connect to a running serving daemon for multi-turn LLM chat.

```
neurobrix chat [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--max-tokens` `MAX_TOKENS` | — | Max tokens per response (default: from model config) |
| `--temperature` `TEMPERATURE` | — | Sampling temperature |
| `--repetition-penalty` `REPETITION_PENALTY` | — | Repetition penalty (1.0 = none) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

```text
Examples:
  neurobrix chat
  neurobrix chat --temperature 0.7
  neurobrix chat --repetition-penalty 1.2

Slash commands (inside chat):
  /new      Start new conversation
  /context  Show token usage
  /status   Show engine status
  /quit     Exit chat
```

## doctor

Diagnose installation problems (PATH, PyTorch/CUDA, GPU visibility).

Check that neurobrix is installed, on PATH, and able to see your GPU. Reports the exact command to fix a PyTorch build that does not match your driver or GPU generation. Exits non-zero when it finds something that will block a real run.

```
neurobrix doctor [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | off | one JSON record on stdout, human lines on stderr (schema in neurobrix/cli/json_out.py) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

## validate

Validate NBX file integrity.

```text
Validate .nbx archive structure and integrity.

Validation levels:
  structure  - Check files exist in ZIP
  schema     - Parse JSON and validate required fields
  coherence  - Cross-reference weights_index with shards (default)
  deep       - Read safetensors headers, verify checksums
```

```
neurobrix validate [options] nbx_files ...
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `nbx_files` | required | Path(s) to .nbx file(s) |
| `--level`, `-l` `{structure,schema,coherence,deep}` | `coherence` | Validation depth (default: coherence) |
| `--strict` | off | Exit on first failure |
| `--json` | off | Output results as JSON |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | off | Show detailed info |

## upscale

Upscale an image using a super-resolution model.

Image super-resolution. Loads an input image, runs it through an upscaler model, writes the high-resolution result.

```
neurobrix upscale [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` `MODEL` | required | Upscaler model name (e.g. swin2SR-realworld-sr-x4-64-bsrgan-psnr) |
| `--input`, `--input-image` `INPUT` | required | Input image path (PNG/JPEG). `--input-image` is accepted as an alias. |
| `--output` `OUTPUT` | required | Output image path (PNG) |
| `--mode` `{compiled,sequential,triton,triton-sequential}` | `compiled` | Execution mode (default: compiled) |
| `--hardware` `HARDWARE` | — | Hardware profile ID (auto-detected if omitted) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

## calibrate

*Developer command: listed by `neurobrix --help -v`, not by `neurobrix --help`.*

Measure the precision calibration record of a model (DtypeEngine fp32 islands).

Run one request on the conservative reference path with the per-op magnitude census installed and write the calibration record every later run derives its fp32 islands from. Same request arguments as `run`; a family without media inputs takes its stimulus from config/families/&lt;family&gt;.yml.

```
neurobrix calibrate [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--time-arms` `N` | `0` | after the census, run the request N times under each arm (conservative, calibrated), keep the least execution time of each and byte-compare the outputs; a calibrated arm that is identical and not faster marks the record "prefer conservative" for this hardware profile |
| `--model` `MODEL` | — | Model name (auto-detected from running daemon if omitted) |
| `--hardware` `HARDWARE` | — | Hardware profile ID (e.g., "v100-32g"). Auto-detected if omitted. |
| `--explain-plan` | off | Print the placement plan — the strategy, why it won and what it beat, every component with its device and memory — then exit without loading anything |
| `--json` | off | with --explain-plan: the plan as one JSON record on stdout |
| `--prompt` `PROMPT` | — | Text prompt for generation |
| `--audio` `AUDIO` | — | Input audio file path (for speech-to-text models) |
| `--steps` `STEPS` | — | Number of inference steps |
| `--cfg` `CFG` | — | Guidance scale |
| `--height` `HEIGHT` | — | Output height in pixels |
| `--width` `WIDTH` | — | Output width in pixels |
| `--output` `OUTPUT` | — | Output file path (default: output.png) |
| `--seed` `SEED` | — | Random seed for reproducibility |
| `--temperature` `TEMPERATURE` | — | Sampling temperature (0 = greedy) |
| `--repetition-penalty` `REPETITION_PENALTY` | — | Repetition penalty (1.0 = none, 1.1-1.5 recommended) |
| `--top-k` `TOP_K` | — | Keep only the k highest-probability tokens (0 = disabled) |
| `--top-p` `TOP_P` | — | Nucleus sampling: keep the smallest set of tokens whose probability sums to p (1.0 = disabled) |
| `--set` `KEY=VALUE` | — | Set arbitrary runtime variable (e.g., --set global.cfg=7.5) |
| `--compiled` | off | PyTorch fused graph + cuDNN/cuBLAS (CompiledSequence). Production PyTorch performance. Used when no execution flag is passed and PyTorch is installed (without it, --triton); this flag makes the choice explicit. |
| `--sequential` | off | PyTorch eager op-by-op (no fusion, ATen dispatcher). Useful for debugging individual ATen ops. Slower than --compiled. |
| `--triton` | off | Triton-pure compiled mode: every op runs on NeuroBrix's own Triton kernels, with no cuDNN or cuBLAS, through a preallocated memory arena and fused kernels (TritonSequence). Needs the triton package. |
| `--triton-sequential` | off | Triton-pure eager mode: Triton kernels op-by-op (no fusion, TritonSequentialDispatcher). Equivalent of --sequential but for the Triton backend. Useful for debugging individual Triton kernels. |
| `--certified-only` | off | Confirmation run: every autotuned kernel is served from the certified directory, or the run fails naming the missing key and its census row — never a runtime sweep, never the local replay cache (NBX_AUTOTUNE_CERTIFIED_ONLY=1). |
| `--max-tokens` `MAX_TOKENS` | — | Maximum number of tokens to generate (LLM only) |
| `--turns` `FILE` | — | A JSON list of user messages played as ONE chat session, turn after turn, through the session code the daemon runs: the KV cache is kept between turns and each turn prefills only its new tokens; each answer is printed (LLM only) |
| `--input-image` `INPUT_IMAGE` | — | Input image path (vlm, img2img, inpainting, upscaler, multimodal) |
| `--input-video` `INPUT_VIDEO` | — | Input video path for understanding (vlm/multimodal) |
| `--mask-image` `MASK_IMAGE` | — | Inpainting mask image path (image inpainting mode) |
| `--reference-image` `REFERENCE_IMAGE` | — | Style reference image (not wired in this version: refused by name) |
| `--reference-audio` `REFERENCE_AUDIO` | — | Voice to clone from a recording (not wired in this version: refused by name) |
| `--speaker` `SPEAKER` | — | Speaker preset id (tts) |
| `--video` `VIDEO` | — | Input video path (video v2v) |
| `--num-frames` `NUM_FRAMES` | — | Number of frames to generate (video) |
| `--fps` `FPS` | — | Output frame rate (video) |
| `--system` `SYSTEM` | — | System prompt for chat-style models (llm, vlm, audio_llm) |
| `--mode` `{auto,text,chat,image,audio,video,t2i,img2img,inpainting,t2v,i2v,v2v}` | — | Execution mode. Required for multimodal (text\|image). Auto-deduced for other families from inputs provided. |
| `--chat` | — | Force chat template formatting |
| `--no-chat` | off | Force raw text completion |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

The certified autotune directory: certify a profile, check the directory, show the status.

```
neurobrix autotune [options] {certify,check,status}
```

|---|---|---|

### autotune certify

*Developer command: listed by `neurobrix --help -v`, not by `neurobrix --help`.*

run every candidate config on every shape the zoo met, against the fp64 oracle; write the files with their proofs.

```
neurobrix autotune certify [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--profile` `PROFILE` | required | the vendor profile this machine carries (its file stem, e.g. volta) |
| `--vendor` `VENDOR` | — | the vendor directory (default: the one in force) |
| `--census` `CENSUS` | — | REFUSED if given: the certifier reads the committed census table of the profile and the card's memory class, nothing else |
| `--out` `OUT` | — | write here instead of the engine directory (a contributor draft) |
| `--kernels` `KERNELS` | — | only these kernels (short or qualified names, comma-separated) |
| `--models` `MODELS` | — | only the census rows of these containers (comma-separated catalogue names): a re-certification takes the keys it needs first |
| `--skip-proven-since` `SKIP_PROVEN_SINCE` | — | skip a key this card's class proved at or after this ISO time (UTC, like the proofs): resume a stopped sweep |
| `--skip-keys` `SKIP_KEYS` | — | a file of "&lt;kernel qualname&gt; &lt;key repr&gt;" lines: keys a resumed sweep has done |
| `--keys` `KEYS` | — | a file of "&lt;kernel qualname&gt;::&lt;key repr&gt;" lines (a coverage check's or a launch record's): certify exactly these keys, not the census table |
| `--limit` `LIMIT` | — | stop after this many shapes |
| `--only-missing` | off | skip shapes the directory already certifies |
| `--working-set-mb` `WORKING_SET_MB` | — | the working-set budget of this run in MiB: every key is priced by its phases before any draw and refused by name over it; pass the figure the run's guard kills at (default: no price door, the operand bound alone) |
| `--allow-uncheckpointed` | off | certify with no checkpointer holding the repository — the proofs then exist only where they are written, which three mains cuts have already cost; say it deliberately or start tools/certified_checkpoint.py |
| `--reprove-unclocked` | off | skip only the shapes certified for this card's class AT A RECORDED CLOCK; a proof that does not say its clock is re-proven at the protocol clock |
| `--reprove-generator` | off | skip only the shapes certified for this card's class UNDER THE RUNNING code generator (the Triton version and the backend hash); a proof made under another one is re-proven by this pass — until then the RUNTIME DOES NOT SERVE IT (a configuration is a property of the compiler that produced it: the shape sweeps at runtime and lands in the local replay cache; NBX_AUTOTUNE_ANY_GENERATOR=1 serves it anyway, at the caller's risk) |
| `--allow-off-protocol-clock` | off | certify even though a card is off this machine's protocol clock (the run says so, and its timings are not comparable with on-protocol ones) |

## drift

*Developer command: listed by `neurobrix --help -v`, not by `neurobrix --help`.*

Name the first op where the Triton engine drifts from the ATen oracle on one request.

Run the same request on the ATen oracle (sequential by default) and on the Triton engine, each writing its per-op record, and name the first op in the oracle's order whose values depart beyond the bound — the site to open. Same request arguments as `run`.

```
neurobrix drift [options]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--out` `OUT` | — | report directory (default ~/.neurobrix/drift/&lt;model&gt;) |
| `--bound` `BOUND` | `0.02` | relative deviation of a per-op window that names a site (default 0.02) |
| `--top` `TOP` | `12` | how many of the largest deviations to list |
| `--oracle` `{sequential,compiled}` | `sequential` | the ATen arm (default: sequential, op by op) |
| `--model` `MODEL` | — | Model name (auto-detected from running daemon if omitted) |
| `--hardware` `HARDWARE` | — | Hardware profile ID (e.g., "v100-32g"). Auto-detected if omitted. |
| `--explain-plan` | off | Print the placement plan — the strategy, why it won and what it beat, every component with its device and memory — then exit without loading anything |
| `--json` | off | with --explain-plan: the plan as one JSON record on stdout |
| `--prompt` `PROMPT` | — | Text prompt for generation |
| `--audio` `AUDIO` | — | Input audio file path (for speech-to-text models) |
| `--steps` `STEPS` | — | Number of inference steps |
| `--cfg` `CFG` | — | Guidance scale |
| `--height` `HEIGHT` | — | Output height in pixels |
| `--width` `WIDTH` | — | Output width in pixels |
| `--output` `OUTPUT` | — | Output file path (default: output.png) |
| `--seed` `SEED` | — | Random seed for reproducibility |
| `--temperature` `TEMPERATURE` | — | Sampling temperature (0 = greedy) |
| `--repetition-penalty` `REPETITION_PENALTY` | — | Repetition penalty (1.0 = none, 1.1-1.5 recommended) |
| `--top-k` `TOP_K` | — | Keep only the k highest-probability tokens (0 = disabled) |
| `--top-p` `TOP_P` | — | Nucleus sampling: keep the smallest set of tokens whose probability sums to p (1.0 = disabled) |
| `--set` `KEY=VALUE` | — | Set arbitrary runtime variable (e.g., --set global.cfg=7.5) |
| `--compiled` | off | PyTorch fused graph + cuDNN/cuBLAS (CompiledSequence). Production PyTorch performance. Used when no execution flag is passed and PyTorch is installed (without it, --triton); this flag makes the choice explicit. |
| `--sequential` | off | PyTorch eager op-by-op (no fusion, ATen dispatcher). Useful for debugging individual ATen ops. Slower than --compiled. |
| `--triton` | off | Triton-pure compiled mode: every op runs on NeuroBrix's own Triton kernels, with no cuDNN or cuBLAS, through a preallocated memory arena and fused kernels (TritonSequence). Needs the triton package. |
| `--triton-sequential` | off | Triton-pure eager mode: Triton kernels op-by-op (no fusion, TritonSequentialDispatcher). Equivalent of --sequential but for the Triton backend. Useful for debugging individual Triton kernels. |
| `--certified-only` | off | Confirmation run: every autotuned kernel is served from the certified directory, or the run fails naming the missing key and its census row — never a runtime sweep, never the local replay cache (NBX_AUTOTUNE_CERTIFIED_ONLY=1). |
| `--max-tokens` `MAX_TOKENS` | — | Maximum number of tokens to generate (LLM only) |
| `--turns` `FILE` | — | A JSON list of user messages played as ONE chat session, turn after turn, through the session code the daemon runs: the KV cache is kept between turns and each turn prefills only its new tokens; each answer is printed (LLM only) |
| `--input-image` `INPUT_IMAGE` | — | Input image path (vlm, img2img, inpainting, upscaler, multimodal) |
| `--input-video` `INPUT_VIDEO` | — | Input video path for understanding (vlm/multimodal) |
| `--mask-image` `MASK_IMAGE` | — | Inpainting mask image path (image inpainting mode) |
| `--reference-image` `REFERENCE_IMAGE` | — | Style reference image (not wired in this version: refused by name) |
| `--reference-audio` `REFERENCE_AUDIO` | — | Voice to clone from a recording (not wired in this version: refused by name) |
| `--speaker` `SPEAKER` | — | Speaker preset id (tts) |
| `--video` `VIDEO` | — | Input video path (video v2v) |
| `--num-frames` `NUM_FRAMES` | — | Number of frames to generate (video) |
| `--fps` `FPS` | — | Output frame rate (video) |
| `--system` `SYSTEM` | — | System prompt for chat-style models (llm, vlm, audio_llm) |
| `--mode` `{auto,text,chat,image,audio,video,t2i,img2img,inpainting,t2v,i2v,v2v}` | — | Execution mode. Required for multimodal (text\|image). Auto-deduced for other families from inputs provided. |
| `--chat` | — | Force chat template formatting |
| `--no-chat` | off | Force raw text completion |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |

## coverage

*Developer command: listed by `neurobrix --help -v`, not by `neurobrix --help`.*

Which installed containers actually reach a symbol.

Census the installed containers for an ATen op or a metadata field. A test that exercises nothing is green, and this answers, before a cell is written, whether a model run can reach the code it claims to validate. It reads graphs, so it answers questions about the graph — never about a runtime decision such as which attention branch was taken, which is chosen while running and is not a node in any graph.

```
neurobrix coverage [options] [OP]
```

| argument | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `OP` | — | an ATen op, with or without the `aten::` prefix |
| `--rarest` `N` | `0` | list the N ops the fewest containers carry |
| `--unreached` | off | ops the engine classifies that NO container carries |
| `--field` `KEY` | — | a container metadata key, and the values declared for it |
| `--json` | off | one JSON record on stdout, human lines on stderr (schema in neurobrix/cli/json_out.py) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | -v: the engine's developer lines; -vv: and the traceback of an error (NBX_LOG=debug: both) |
